sheets.title: MATCH-WEEK GUIDE – WHAT TO DO ON WHICH DAY (1 match a week)
sheets.sub: MD = match day. MD-4 = 4 days to the match. MD+1 = 1 day after the match. Look at the day cards first, then the coloured table.

rows.lab: Example day (if the match is on Sunday)

vals:
SPEED DAY
(short, sharp, plenty of rest)
Starters: light recovery. Non-starters: game + running to compensate for match load
Small-sided games, acceleration-deceleration, change of direction (mechanical load)
Large-area game, high-speed running, max velocity (locomotor load)
Upper body. Non-starters: lower-body top-up + Nordic / Copenhagen
MAIN LOWER-BODY STRENGTH: heavy compound 3-5 reps + few jumps. Copenhagen at the end
POWER (weightlifting, jumps, med ball) + upper body. Nordic
Core + balance, short isometrics, very few jumps
High-rep hypertrophy (soreness carries into the match)
High-volume lower body, new / unfamiliar exercises

rows.lab: Hip dominant (KD): RDL, deadlift, hip thrust
rows.note: Main lift on MD-4. MD+1 non-starters only.
On MD-3. MD+1 top-up for non-starters.
End of MD-4 session. MD-2 isometric only.
Seated (soleus) work is key for sprinting.
Jump shrug, hang clean: low reps.

items.text: Framework: tactical periodisation week (strength – endurance – speed days; Delgado-Bordonau & Mendez-Villanueva 2012), Buchheit et al. 2021 (mechanical / locomotor load split).

sheets.title: POSITION-SPECIFIC WEEKLY MICRO-DOSE PROGRAMS
sheets.sub: Ready short sessions for every day of the match week for centre-backs, full-backs, defensive and central midfielders, wingers, strikers and goalkeepers.

items.text: Short (5-20 min) micro-dose sessions for 5 days of the match week, for each position. One match a week is assumed; MD+2 is a day off. The MD+1 session is for players who played; non-starters can use the MD-4 session. Adjust loads to the player's level, lower the volume as the match approaches and keep the speed. BW = bodyweight · /s = each side. Framework: Di Salvo 2007, Bradley 2009, Harper 2019, Oliva-Lozano 2023 (positional demands); Cuthbert 2024 (micro-dosing); Rønnestad 2011 (in-season strength maintenance); van der Horst 2015, Harøy 2019 (Nordic, Copenhagen); Buchheit 2021 (match-week distribution).
Aerial and physical duels, high deceleration and recovery runs; less high-speed running than other positions. Priority: vertical power (headers), posterior-chain strength, braking, neck and trunk.
items.text_en: Aerial and physical duels, high deceleration and recovery runs; less high-speed running than other positions. Priority: vertical power (headers), posterior-chain strength, braking, neck and trunk.

sheets.title: READY PROGRAMS – 7-DAY WEEK (1 match a week)
sheets.sub: 3 models: choose one based on the team's facilities and the coach's set-up. Each model shows the weekly plan first, then the gym sessions day by day.

items.title: MODEL 1 – CLASSIC: 2 main gym sessions (MD-4 lower-body strength + MD-3 power and upper body)
items.text: For: teams with 30-45 min of gym twice a week. Logic: heavy lower body on the loading day furthest from the match (MD-4), power and upper body on MD-3, only core on MD-2, primer on MD-1.

rows.gym: Upper body + lower-body top-up for non-starters

rows.field: Endurance day: large area, high-speed running

items.title: MODEL 1 · MD+1 – Upper body + top-up for non-starters
items.text: Everyone does blocks A and B. Block C is only for non-starters and players who played under 45 min.

items.title: MODEL 1 · MD-4 – Main lower-body strength
items.text: The most important gym session of the week. Quality in the main lift (B1): every rep fast and clean. ~12 heavy sets in total.

items.title: MODEL 1 · MD-3 – Power + upper body + Nordic
MODEL 1 · MD-1 – Primer
items.text: Day before the match: wake up the nervous system, don't fatigue it. 5-8 min.

items.title: MODEL 2 – STRENGTH / ENDURANCE / SPEED DAYS (tactical periodisation): one main gym session
items.text: For: staff who build field training around day themes. Logic: gym work complements the field theme. One main session on the strength day (MD-4), only short prevention on the endurance day, a speed-power primer on the speed day.

rows.field: STRENGTH day: small area, lots of stop-start, short bouts
ENDURANCE day: large area, long bouts
SPEED day: max velocity, short actions, long rests

items.title: MODEL 2 · MD+1 – Recovery + core
items.text: Low intensity. Aim: circulation, range of motion and trunk control.

items.title: MODEL 2 · MD-4 – Whole-body strength (the week's only main session)
items.text: Lower and upper body are paired: one works while the other rests, so the session is shorter.

items.title: MODEL 2 · MD-3 – Short prevention
items.text: Only 3 movements. Hamstring, calf and trunk.

items.title: MODEL 2 · MD-2 – Speed-power primer
items.text: Light, fast, few reps. Recover fully between reps.

items.title: MODEL 2 · MD-1 – Primer
items.text: 5 min. Final stimulus before the match.

items.title: MODEL 3 – MICRO-DOSE: 15-20 min every day
items.text: For: teams with no separate gym time or a small gym. Logic: split the weekly work into small parts; 3-4 movements every day.

items.title: MODEL 3 · MD-2 – Isometrics + core micro-dose
items.text: 12 min. Isometric work leaves no soreness.

sheets.title: READY PROGRAMS – 8-DAY WEEK (8 days between matches)
sheets.sub: A long week is a development opportunity: an extra loading day (MD-5) is gained. 2 models.

items.title: MODEL 1 – TWO LOWER-BODY STIMULI: MD-5 volume + MD-4 heavy and short
items.text: For: teams wanting to develop strength. Logic: higher-volume lower-body session on MD-5, short heavy stimulus + upper body on MD-4, power on MD-3.

items.title: 8 DAYS · MODEL 1 · MD+1 – Upper body + top-up
items.text: Block C is for non-starters only.

items.title: 8 DAYS · MODEL 1 · MD-5 – Lower-body strength A (volume)
items.text: Highest-volume session of the week. With 5 days to the match, some soreness is tolerated.

items.title: 8 DAYS · MODEL 1 · MD-4 – Heavy-short lower body + upper body
items.text: Only one heavy lower-body lift: low volume, high load.

items.title: MODEL 2 – DEVELOPMENT WEEK: one main whole-body session on MD-5
items.text: For: teams with one long gym session a week. Logic: biggest load on MD-5 (furthest from the match); MD-4 prevention only, MD-3 power. For MD+1 use Model 1's MD+1 session.

items.title: 8 DAYS · MODEL 2 · MD-5 – Whole-body strength (main session)
items.text: Progresses in lower-upper pairs. ~22 working sets in total.

items.title: 8 DAYS · MODEL 2 · MD-4 – Prevention only
items.text: Gym is short because field load is high.

items.title: 8 DAYS · MODEL 2 · MD-3 – Power + upper body

sheets.title: READY PROGRAMS – 2 MATCHES A WEEK (a match every 3-4 days)
sheets.sub: No single program in congested fixtures: starters and non-starters train separately. 3 models.

items.title: MODEL 1 – STARTERS (60+ min): recover + micro-dose
items.text: Logic: the match itself is the biggest load. The gym's job is to maintain strength without hurting freshness: isometrics and low-rep concentric work, no eccentrics or volume.

items.title: 2 MATCHES · STARTERS · MD+1 – Recovery circuit
items.text: Low intensity. Upper body kept light, no lower-body load.

items.title: 2 MATCHES · STARTERS · MD-2 – Micro-dose isometrics + core
items.text: 10-15 min. Isometric: high-force stimulus without soreness or fatigue.

items.title: MODEL 2 – NON-STARTERS and LOW MINUTES (under 45 min): top-up
items.text: Logic: players who miss the match load lose strength and power. On the day after the match (MD+1) a lower-body strength-power session and compensatory running on the field are done. Sessions A and B alternate.

items.title: 2 MATCHES · NON-STARTERS · MD+1 – Top-up A (vertical: knee dominant + jumps)
2 MATCHES · NON-STARTERS · MD+1 – Top-up B (horizontal: hip dominant + sprint power)
2 MATCHES · NON-STARTERS · MD-2 – Short strength
items.text: 15 min. A non-starter can also do short heavy work on MD-2 (if unlikely to play next day).

items.title: MODEL 3 – VERY CONGESTED (3 matches in 7 days): maintenance only
items.text: Logic: no new stimulus. A 12-min maintenance circuit the day after the match, a primer the day before. Strength loss is limited for up to 2-3 weeks; return to Model 1 when the schedule opens up.

items.title: 2 MATCHES · CONGESTED · Day after match – 12-min maintenance circuit
2 MATCHES · CONGESTED · Day before match – Primer

sheets.title: WARM-UP – PREPARATION (based on the day's content)
sheets.sub: Rule: the day's field content sets the warm-up. Stop-start day (MD-4) → INTENSIVE. Max-velocity day (MD-3) → EXTENSIVE. Day before the match → PRIMER. Each 10-12 min, in order: mobility → movement preparation → isometric stimulus → specific preparation → primer.

items.title: INTENSIVE – Acceleration and deceleration day (MD-4)
items.text: Anterior-chain and thoracic mobility, lunge-squat pattern, braking patterns. Daily readiness is monitored with a CMJ at the end.

items.title: EXTENSIVE – Max-velocity day (MD-3)
items.text: Posterior-chain and ankle mobility, single-leg RDL and bridge, hamstring stimulus, running mechanics.

items.title: MD-1 – Primer and power
items.text: General mobility + a few maximal jumps. Wakes you up without fatigue.

items.title: FIFA 11+ style injury-prevention warm-up (2-3 times a week)
items.text: Running drills → strength, balance, jumping → fast running. Shown to reduce lower-limb injuries when done regularly (Soligard 2008).

sheets.title: TRAINING METHODS – CONTRAST, COMPLEX, FRENCH CONTRAST AND OTHERS
sheets.sub: For each method: what it is, how it is done, when it is used and ready sample programs. Common idea (contrast family): a heavy lift excites the nervous system, so an explosive movement performed right after is more powerful (post-activation performance enhancement, PAPE).

items.title: 1 · CONTRAST (heavy ↔ explosive, alternating set by set)
items.what: A heavy strength movement is paired with an explosive movement of the same pattern: 1 heavy set, 1 explosive set, then heavy again.
items.how: A1 heavy set (80-90%, 2-4 reps) → wait 20-60 s → A2 explosive set (bodyweight or light load, 3-5 reps) → rest 2-3 min → A1 again. 3-4 rounds.
items.when: Pre-season weeks 4-6, in-season MD-4 / MD-3. More effective in players with a strength base (squat ≥ 1.5 x bodyweight).

items.title: CONTRAST · Program 2 – Lower body, horizontal (sprint power)
2 · ASCENDING COMPLEX (light-fast first, then heavy)
items.what: ALL sets of the explosive / light movements are done first, the heavy lift comes last.
items.how: All sets of A (explosive) → all sets of B (moderate load, fast) → all sets of C (heavy). No pairing: each movement on its own, full rest between sets.
items.when: If speed and power are the priority (MD-3, in-season). Do the fastest work first while the nervous system is fresh.

items.title: 3 · DESCENDING COMPLEX (heavy first, then light-fast)
items.what: ALL sets of the heavy lift are done first, then the load drops and movements get faster.
items.how: All sets of A (heavy) → all sets of B (moderate load, fast) → all sets of C (bodyweight, explosive). Later movements benefit from the stimulus of the heavy sets.
items.when: If strength is the priority (MD-4, pre-season).

items.title: DESCENDING · Program 1 – Lower body, hip dominant
DESCENDING · Program 2 – Lower body, knee dominant and lateral
4 · FRENCH CONTRAST (4 movements back to back)
items.what: 4 movements of the same pattern back to back: heavy compound → plyometric → lightly loaded fast movement → assisted (or very fast) plyometric.
items.how: A1 → 20 s → A2 → 20 s → A3 → 20 s → A4 → rest 3-5 min between rounds. 2-4 rounds. Short rest within, long rest between rounds.
items.when: Advanced players with a solid strength base. Final pre-season weeks. In-season only 2 rounds and MD-4 / MD-3.

items.title: FRENCH CONTRAST · Program 1 – Vertical (jump)
items.text: Squat → hurdle jump → loaded jump → band-assisted jump.

items.title: FRENCH CONTRAST · Program 2 – Yatay (sprint)
items.text: Hip thrust → broad jump → resisted sprint → free sprint.

items.title: FRENCH CONTRAST · Program 3 – Upper body
items.text: Bench press → plyometric push-up → speed bench → band-assisted push-up.

items.title: 5 · CLUSTER SET (mini rests within the set)
items.what: A set is split into small parts with 15-30 s mini rests. More high-quality (fast) reps are done with the same heavy load.
items.how: Example 2+2+2: 2 reps → rack the bar, 20 s → 2 reps → 20 s → 2 reps = 1 set. 3 min between sets. Load 85-90%.
items.when: In maximal strength and power blocks. Useful in-season too because it limits velocity loss.

items.title: 6 · SUPERSET (opposing muscle groups paired)
items.what: A push is paired with a pull, or an anterior with a posterior-chain movement. One rests while the other works.
items.how: A1 → 45-60 s → A2 → 45-60 s → A1 again. The same work is done in less time; internal load and perceived fatigue rise slightly.
items.when: When time is limited. MD+1 upper-body sessions, pre-season volume weeks.

items.title: SUPERSET · Program 2 – Lower body (anterior ↔ posterior chain)
7 · ECCENTRIC EMPHASIS (slow lowering, flywheel)
items.what: The lowering (lengthening) phase is emphasised: slow tempo or a flywheel (isoinertial) device.
items.how: Tempo: 4-5 s lowering, no pause, fast rise. Flywheel: pull fast, brake late and hard on the return. Causes soreness: at least 4 days before the match.
items.when: For deceleration capacity and hamstring / adductor protection. Pre-season, MD-4 / MD-5.

items.title: 8 · ISOMETRIC (maximal push without movement)
items.what: Maximal force is applied for 3-5 s against an immovable resistance (pins, fixed bar). Gives a high-force stimulus without soreness or fatigue.
items.how: 3-5 x 3-5 s maximal push, 45-60 s between. An explosive movement of the same pattern can follow (isometric ↔ explosive contrast).
items.when: Congested fixtures, MD-2, MD-1 and early phases of return from injury.

items.text: Source: Cormier et al. 2022 (classification of complex and contrast training).
